processRules: Absolute executable and working directory, explicit environment, no shell and hidden Windows window.
Bound input, stdout, stderr and wall time. Snapshot input bytes before sending them.
Classify timeout, cancellation and output/input limits as resource exhaustion; process crashes are not semantic rejection.
Require process termination confirmation. Unknown CPU, memory and host-stack measurements remain null.
Successful process exit returns untrusted bytes and has no kernel authority.
producerRules: Only a local runtime endpoint and an explicitly pinned, already-present image digest are allowed; no implicit pull.
Require a Linux image for the selected architecture and reject image-declared writable volumes.
Disable network, host mounts, ambient credential forwarding, health checks and host log accumulation.
Use a non-root user, read-only root, dropped capabilities, no-new-privileges and bounded scratch, memory, swap, processes and CPU allocation.
On completion or failure, remove only this invocation's random container name and confirm absence if removal reports failure.
limitations: A process wrapper alone does not isolate descendants, memory or CPU.
Container/runtime/OS hardening is an external assumption and does not upgrade ProviderSecurityProfile or enable the paranoid profile.
Local checks exercise real bounded child processes and mock container orchestration. No real container execution or escape-resistance claim is made.
Integration with the complete challenge/export/statement/assumption/checker comparator protocol remains required.
Compiler-wide resource coverage and monotonicity remain incomplete/unproved.
